subject: Regional availability carve-out and staged failover proposal for Nimbus Health
messages:
From: Jasdeep Singh <jasdeep@nimbushealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-12-01T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Request: multi-region RTO/RPO guarantees for production EHR flows

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving toward a production pilot for patient-facing summaries and need to lock down availability guarantees before procurement can sign off. Nimbus' security and ops teams have a hard requirement for multi-region failover across US-EAST and US-WEST with the following asks:

- RTO <= 5 minutes for stateless API requests on failover
- RPO = 0 for telemetry and audit logs (no loss)
- Maintain 99.9% request success across regions; 99th percentile latency <= 300ms under normal operation

We understand there are trade-offs; please confirm whether Redwood can commit to these in the Enterprise SOW or whether an exception/carveout is required. If a carveout is necessary, we need the alternate SLOs plus remediation and credit language to move forward.

Attached is a redlined SOW template for reference.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is targeting next-week approval.

Regards,
Jasdeep
Director of IT Operations
Nimbus Health

Attachment: nimbus-requested-sla-draft.docx (docx, 360KB)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Jasdeep Singh <jasdeep@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-01T12:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region RTO/RPO guarantees for production EHR flows

Jasdeep —

Thanks for the clear asks and the SOW. Short answer: we can meet the stateless API RTO target in most cases but we cannot guarantee RPO=0 for telemetry and audit logs without specific replication plumbing in your architecture. A few quick points and a proposed staged alternative:

1) Stateless API RTO: For purely stateless calls (no session KV), our multi-region warm standby + automated DNS failover can deliver failover detection and routing in ~30–90s; full capacity recovery to 95% depends on model warmup and cache state. We can commit to an RTO target of <=3 minutes for the ingress routing and <=15 minutes for full throughput recovery for a standard Dedicated configuration.

2) Stateful/KV-backed requests & RPO: We do not provide synchronous cross-region write replication by default. Audit/telemetry with RPO=0 would require either: synchronous replication to a customer-managed replica (recommended), or Redwood-managed active-active session replication (extra-cost add-on). Without that, worst-case RPO for in-flight KV writes during a region outage is non-zero; we typically size this at an expected window of up to 5 minutes for write buffers that haven't been flushed.

3) Latency SLOs: Our 99th percentile latency across regional endpoints is normally <= 300ms for supported models and standard token budgets. During failover we expect elevated latencies; proposal below captures that.

Proposed staged failover carveout (for SOW):
- Detection & routing: <= 90s
- Stateless API RTO (warm routing + partial capacity): <= 3 minutes (95th percentile of simulated events)
- Full capacity recovery (including model warmup, KV cache rebuild): <= 15 minutes
- RPO for telemetry/audit without synchronous replication: best effort; typical window <= 5 minutes. If RPO=0 is contractually required, Redwood will include an add-on for synchronous replication with architecture work and a 6–8 week delivery timeline.

We can include credits if we miss the staged targets (credit table in attached PDF). I've summarized this in the attached proposal.

Would you be available for a short call today to walk procurement through the trade-offs?

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-staged-failover-proposal.pdf (pdf, 85KB)

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
To: Jasdeep Singh <jasdeep@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-12-01T15:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region RTO/RPO guarantees for production EHR flows

Jasdeep — looping in Legal and Solutions so we can operationalize the carveout cleanly. Two quick clarifications that will shape the SOW language:

- Scope: Are you intending Redwood to manage audit/telemetry storage (we host) or will you be pushing telemetry to your managed store? If you host, we can implement synchronous replication options. If you host, our recommended pattern is pushing telemetry via Kafka/Firehose where you own replication semantics.
- Acceptable fallback latency: is an elevated latency of up to 700ms P99 during failover acceptable for client UX, given a short period while caches and model quantization warm?

Ben — can you validate how Dedicated config + model pinning affects cold-start time assumptions? Neha — please call out any security/compliance notes if we recommend a replication add-on.

Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Jasdeep Singh <jasdeep@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.ai>, Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-12-02T10:30:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region RTO/RPO guarantees for production EHR flows

Jasdeep — following up with concrete numbers from infra:

- Warm standby + sticky KV: typical DNS failover + routing = 30–90s. For endpoints that are purely stateless we see median RTO ~45s in our last tabletop tests.
- Full throughput depends on model size and tokenizer warmup: for our recommended medium-sized LLMs (7B–13B quantized) full throughput for concurrent sessions typically returns within 8–12 minutes, 95th percentile up to 15 minutes.
- RPO: audit logs that are persisted to our managed logging tier have near-real-time replication within the same region; cross-region synchronous replication is not currently GA. With the add-on (design/engineering work) we can achieve practical RPO <=1s. Without it, design assumption is potential loss of up to 5 minutes of volatile write buffers.

If Nimbus requires RPO=0 and the synchronous replication add-on we will: 1) scope engineering work, 2) estimate cost and timeline (rough ballpark: $65k engineering + infra delta, 6–8 weeks), and 3) add explicit credit terms in the SOW for staged targets.

I'll produce a short amendment template for procurement to review.

—Ben
Principal Solutions Architect
Redwood Inference

From: Jasdeep Singh <jasdeep@nimbushealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Nimbus Health Procurement <procurement@nimbushealth.com>, Aria Gomez <aria.gomez@nimbushealth.com>
Date: 2027-12-03T09:00:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Request: multi-region RTO/RPO guarantees for production EHR flows

Thanks — that framing helps a lot. Procurement is OK with the staged failover language provided Redwood includes:

- A defined add-on path priced/committed in the SOW for synchronous cross-region replication to achieve RPO=0 (approximate numbers are acceptable in the amendment)
- Credit table tied to the staged targets you listed (detection, stateless RTO, full capacity recovery)
- A 30-day SLA review window after go-live to validate assumptions and tune replication/caching rules

We can accept a P99 latency up to 700ms during the 15-minute recovery window if credits apply when thresholds are missed. Please send the amendment + redlined SOW and we will route to legal and procurement for signature.

I'll expect the draft amendment by EOD tomorrow.

-Jasdeep
Director of IT Operations
Nimbus Health
